speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by clarifying your timeline: when exactly did you first notice the gait instability and limb incoordination, and have these symptoms been gradually worsening? Additionally, do you have a known history of autoimmune disorders, prior infections, or significant alcohol use?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That "drunk" appearance is concerning for cerebellar involvement; are your symptoms constant, or do they worsen significantly when you move your eyes or focus on a target? Also, have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your limbs, and do you have a history of diabetes or vitamin deficiencies?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. I am requesting MRI images of the brain to confirm the presence of non-enhancing white matter lesions.
